scenes.title:
Before permissions,
inspect the decision.
scenes.body: A local test bench for onchain agents.
lines: Known state
Changed decision
Reproducible evidence
narration: Before an onchain agent gets production permissions, its decisions need a reproducible test.
Entrotter lets a developer start from known blockchain state, change a decision, and keep a record another developer can inspect.

scenes.title:
A passing simulation
is only the beginning.
scenes.body: The proposed problem: experiments become hard to review when their context is lost.
lines: Which block and overrides?
What did the policy actually see?
Can a teammate reproduce the result?
narration: A passing simulation alone does not explain a decision. Which block did it use? Which balances were overridden? What information reached the policy?
Our hypothesis is that teams need these answers together, instead of scattered across scripts, terminal logs, and screenshots.

scenes.title:
Fork. Compare.
Record. Replay.
scenes.body: Real Anvil execution, explicit assumptions and a content-addressed JSON result.
lines: Paired branches start from the same state
Policy can hold or execute the exact proposal
Replay refuses changed observations
narration: Entrotter runs baseline and candidate actions from identical initial state in separate Anvil instances. A constrained policy sees the current proposal, current state, and completed actions, not future steps.
It can hold, or execute the unchanged proposal. The report keeps source pins, receipts, token units, assumptions, and the recorded decisions.

scenes.title:
19 reports.
19 exact reproductions.
scenes.body: 16 archived-state executions + 3 local cases. 12 agent records replayed. No new model calls.
lines: 189 native and unit tests
21 real Docker tests
CPU, memory and lifetime bounds
narration: The current review branch reproduces all nineteen existing EVM reports as exactly equal complete artifacts, including twelve agent recordings, without calling a model again.
One hundred eighty nine native and unit tests, and twenty one real Docker tests, verify behavior and resource controls. All results and limitations are public.

scenes.eyebrow: WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT SAY
scenes.title:
No claimed model edge.
No claimed speed edge.
scenes.body: Negative results are part of the product, not something to hide.
lines: Recorded model matched the risk rule in five cases
Direct Anvil 8.653 s · Entrotter 8.689 s median
Token balance changes are not profit
narration: The model matched the deterministic risk rule in the five evaluated historical cases, and took longer. A same-task comparison also showed no speed advantage over a direct Anvil script.
The proposed value is a reusable, reviewable experiment and replay record. It is not a claim of smarter trading, future prediction, or profit.

scenes.title:
For teams reviewing
onchain agent decisions.
scenes.body: Start with EVM agent developers who already build their own simulation scripts.
lines: Local execution and private report files
Versioned scenarios that fit code review
Three independent user sessions planned
narration: The initial audience is small EVM agent teams that already write simulation scripts and need a teammate to reproduce a questionable decision.

The first validation target is three genuine developer sessions: run their own case, reproduce a colleague's result, and identify what would make this workflow useful. Those sessions have not happened yet.

scenes.title:
Free OSS core.
Test paid team value.
scenes.body: A pricing experiment, not an available product or proven willingness to pay.
lines: MIT local engine and report viewer
Hypothesis: shared reviews and scenario management
Interview anchor: $99 / team / month
narration: The local engine and viewer are MIT licensed. A business hypothesis is paid team collaboration around shared scenarios and reviews, while local execution stays open source.
Ninety nine dollars per team per month is an interview anchor, not a live offer or validated willingness to pay. There are no verified customer or revenue claims.

scenes.title:
Bring one decision
you need to explain.
lines: Run locally · inspect an artifact · contribute a failure case
Current integration requires independent review
Synthetic narration · Codex-assisted work disclosed
narration: Start with the public example, inspect the assumptions, then bring one decision you need to explain. The site and six repositories provide the code and measured evidence.
The bounded agent integration still needs independent review. Team details and demand validation remain pending. This presentation uses synthetic narration and discloses Codex assisted development.
